_comment: Batch 07 (Sets 12-13). Distractor-only rewrites to remove the longest-answer cue. Correct options, stems, and rationales are unchanged; each distractor keeps its original meaning and stays wrong for the same reason. RN-S13-15 (single-word antidote names) is in skipped.json.

RN-S12-01.B: A client 1 day postpartum whose fundus is firm at the umbilicus with a moderate amount of rubra lochia
RN-S12-01.C: A client at 32 weeks' gestation who reports a mild backache after standing at work for several hours
RN-S12-01.D: A newborn with bluish hands and feet 1 hour after birth whose heart rate and breathing are within normal limits

RN-S12-04.A: Gently push the exposed loop of cord back into the vagina using a sterile, lubricated gloved hand
RN-S12-04.C: Place the client in high-Fowler's position and call the provider to the bedside
RN-S12-04.D: Wrap the exposed cord in dry gauze and keep the client still until the provider arrives

RN-S12-08.A: Painless, bright red vaginal bleeding with a soft, nontender, relaxed uterus
RN-S12-08.C: Irregular, painless contractions that ease with rest and hydration
RN-S12-08.D: A steady trickle of clear fluid from the vagina with no pain or bleeding

RN-S12-09.A: No treatment is needed because the Coombs test is negative
RN-S12-09.C: Administering Rh immune globulin to the newborn within 72 hours
RN-S12-09.D: Administering the rubella vaccine instead of Rh immune globulin

RN-S12-10.A: Increase the oxytocin rate to strengthen labor
RN-S12-10.C: Encourage the client to begin pushing with each contraction
RN-S12-10.D: Document the findings as an expected response

RN-S12-13.A: Pinkish-brown lochia serosa, a firm fundus at the midline, and mild incisional soreness
RN-S12-13.C: Cramping afterpains during breastfeeding that are relieved by the prescribed ibuprofen
RN-S12-13.D: Bilateral breast fullness and tenderness as the client's milk comes in on day 3

RN-S12-15.A: "It's given to prevent eye infections that the baby could have picked up while passing through the birth canal."
RN-S12-15.C: "It prevents jaundice, which many healthy newborns develop during the first week after birth."
RN-S12-15.D: "It boosts the immune system so your baby can fight off infections in the first weeks."

RN-S12-18.A: The newborn feeds every 5–6 hours and sleeps well between feedings
RN-S12-18.C: The newborn cries and fusses after every feeding during the day
RN-S12-18.D: The mother's breasts never feel full before or after feedings

RN-S13-01.A: A 3-year-old with croup who has a barking cough and no stridor at rest after a dose of dexamethasone
RN-S13-01.C: An 8-year-old with a casted forearm fracture who rates pain 5/10 and is due for an oral analgesic
RN-S13-01.D: A 6-month-old who is due for scheduled immunizations and is feeding well with the parent at the bedside

RN-S13-04.A: A mild cold with a runny nose and a temperature of 99.8°F (37.7°C)
RN-S13-04.C: Currently taking amoxicillin for an ear infection diagnosed 3 days ago
RN-S13-04.D: A sibling at home who is pregnant and due to deliver next month

RN-S13-06.A: Administer the dose as prescribed, since it is within the safe range for the child's weight
RN-S13-06.C: Administer half the dose and document the reason in the child's medication record
RN-S13-06.D: Give the dose every 12 hours instead of every 8 hours to lower the daily total

RN-S13-07.A: "We'll get the MMR vaccine next week as scheduled at the pediatrician's office."
RN-S13-07.C: "We can give ibuprofen along with the aspirin if our child gets a fever at home."
RN-S13-07.D: "The peeling skin on the fingers and toes means the treatment didn't work."

RN-S13-08.A: Proceed with the air enema procedure as scheduled
RN-S13-08.C: Offer the infant a bottle of formula before the procedure
RN-S13-08.D: Document the normal stool in the infant's chart only

RN-S13-09.B: Currant jelly stools with episodes of severe abdominal pain and drawn-up knees
RN-S13-09.C: Bile-stained vomitus with metabolic acidosis and a distended abdomen
RN-S13-09.D: Failure to pass meconium in the first 48 hours after birth, with abdominal distention

RN-S13-10.A: Passing meconium within 24 hours of birth with a soft abdomen
RN-S13-10.C: Yellow, seedy stools by day 4 in a newborn who is breastfeeding well
RN-S13-10.D: Greenish-brown transitional stools on day 3 with a soft, flat, nontender abdomen

RN-S13-12.B: Lay the child flat on the back in the crib
RN-S13-12.C: Encourage the child to walk around the room
RN-S13-12.D: Give the child a bottle of juice to calm down

RN-S13-17.A: Palpate the abdomen every 4 hours to monitor the tumor's size
RN-S13-17.C: Encourage the child to lie prone to reduce abdominal discomfort
RN-S13-17.D: Apply a warm pack to the abdomen to relieve the child's discomfort

RN-S13-18.A: "I'll wear it only at night while I'm sleeping and take it off before I go to school."
RN-S13-18.C: "I'll wear it only while I'm playing sports so my back is supported during games."
RN-S13-18.D: "I'll stop wearing it if it becomes uncomfortable or rubs against my skin."

RN-S13-19.A: Tell the parents not to visit for the next few days, because seeing them leave each night upsets the child
RN-S13-19.C: Ask the provider for a sedative to calm the child after the parents leave each night
RN-S13-19.D: Tell the child firmly to stop crying because the other children on the unit are sleeping

PN-S12-02.A: "Taking folic acid every day helps prevent the morning sickness that many people have in the first trimester."
PN-S12-02.C: "Folic acid helps prevent gestational diabetes, which usually develops later in pregnancy."
PN-S12-02.D: "Folic acid is only needed after the baby is born, to help you recover and make breast milk."

PN-S12-07.A: "Count the baby's movements for 5 minutes once a week, and call if you feel fewer than 3."
PN-S12-07.C: "Only count the baby's movements while you are up and walking around during the day, not while you're resting."
PN-S12-07.D: "Fetal movement doesn't need to be monitored at this stage unless you have a high-risk pregnancy."

PN-S12-08.A: About 5 cm (3 fingerbreadths) above the umbilicus
PN-S12-08.C: Just above the level of the symphysis pubis
PN-S12-08.D: Not palpable above the level of the symphysis pubis

PN-S12-09.A: Notify the provider and wait for prescriptions before touching the uterus
PN-S12-09.C: Give the client oral fluids and recheck the fundus in 30 minutes
PN-S12-09.D: Document the finding and recheck the fundus at the next assessment

PN-S12-11.B: "Apply warm heat packs to the perineum for the first 24 hours to ease the soreness."
PN-S12-11.C: "Use tampons instead of pads for the lochia once the heavy flow slows down."
PN-S12-11.D: "After each time you void, wipe from back to front with soft toilet tissue."

PN-S12-12.A: "Stop breastfeeding for a day or two until the swelling and pain in your breasts go down."
PN-S12-12.C: "Bind your breasts tightly with an elastic wrap to reduce the swelling and pain."
PN-S12-12.D: "Skip the night feedings so your breasts have time to rest and the swelling eases."

PN-S12-13.A: "Pump your breasts a few times a day to relieve the fullness and pressure."
PN-S12-13.C: "Take warm showers with the water directed at your breasts to ease the pain."
PN-S12-13.D: "Massage your breasts frequently to soften them and relieve the pain."

PN-S12-14.A: "Wipe the base of the cord with rubbing alcohol 6 times a day to help it dry out and fall off sooner."
PN-S12-14.C: "If it hasn't fallen off on its own, gently pull the cord off when the baby is 3 days old."
PN-S12-14.D: "Cover the cord with a snug bandage and tape to keep it clean and protected until it falls off."

PN-S12-16.A: Apical heart rate of 138/min while the newborn is sleeping
PN-S12-16.D: Periodic breathing with pauses under 10 seconds during sleep

PN-S12-18.A: Bathe the newborn right away to remove the vernix, blood, and amniotic fluid from the skin
PN-S12-18.C: Place the newborn in a bassinet near an open window for fresh air while the mother rests
PN-S12-18.D: Leave the newborn wet and uncovered under the overhead light while the Apgar score is assessed

PN-S12-21.A: "You should be happy right now. You have a beautiful, healthy baby to take home, so try to focus on that instead of crying all the time."
PN-S12-21.C: "Crying all the time like this means you have postpartum depression, and you will need to start medication for it."
PN-S12-21.D: "Try your best not to cry in front of the baby, because babies can pick up on their mother's moods and become fussy."

PN-S12-22.A: "It protects this baby from developing jaundice during the first few days after birth."
PN-S12-22.C: "It treats the anemia you developed from the blood you lost during the delivery."
PN-S12-22.D: "It's a vaccine that protects you and your future babies against rubella infection."

PN-S12-23.A: "No, breastfeeding always prevents pregnancy, so you don't need to use any other form of birth control while nursing."
PN-S12-23.C: "You can't ovulate for a full year after giving birth, whether or not you are breastfeeding your baby."
PN-S12-23.D: "Only mothers who are formula-feeding their babies need to think about contraception in the first year."

PN-S13-04.A: "Give acetaminophen and check the temperature again tomorrow."
PN-S13-04.C: "Give a lukewarm sponge bath and continue to monitor at home."
PN-S13-04.D: "This is a normal temperature for a baby right after feeding."

PN-S13-06.A: "Prop the bottle on a rolled blanket so that your baby can feed independently."
PN-S13-06.C: "Give the bottle at bedtime while the baby is lying down in the crib."
PN-S13-06.D: "Clean inside the ear canals with cotton swabs every day after the bath."

PN-S13-07.A: "You only need to go to the emergency room if your child's barking cough lasts for more than a week."
PN-S13-07.C: "Go to the emergency room if your child develops a runny nose or a mild fever."
PN-S13-07.D: "Go to the emergency room if your child starts coughing more during the night."

PN-S13-08.A: Green zone: continue the usual daily controller medications as prescribed
PN-S13-08.C: Red zone: call 911 or go to the emergency department immediately
PN-S13-08.D: The meter is broken and should be replaced before the next reading

PN-S13-09.A: After lunch, once the child has used the toilet and washed
PN-S13-09.C: Right after the child's evening bath, before bed
PN-S13-09.D: At bedtime, right after the child brushes their teeth

PN-S13-10.A: "Make your child vomit right away by gently putting a finger down the back of the throat."
PN-S13-10.C: "Give your child a large glass of milk to dilute it, then wait and watch."
PN-S13-10.D: "Wait at home to see whether any symptoms develop over the next few hours."

PN-S13-11.A: "You can turn the car seat around to face forward once your child turns 12 months old and weighs at least 20 pounds."
PN-S13-11.C: "You can turn the car seat to face forward as soon as your child can sit up without any help."
PN-S13-11.D: "You can turn the car seat to face forward once your child is walking well on their own."

PN-S13-13.A: Reaching 12 months of age, regardless of any other readiness signs
PN-S13-13.C: Can count to 10 and recite most of the alphabet without help
PN-S13-13.D: Sleeps through the night without waking up for a feeding

PN-S13-14.A: "Give your child whatever they want so the tantrum stops as quickly as possible."
PN-S13-14.C: "Spank your child firmly so that they learn tantrums are not allowed."
PN-S13-14.D: "Lock your child in a room by themselves until they have calmed down."

PN-S13-15.A: Assigning the teen to a room with a toddler who has a similar illness
PN-S13-15.C: Having the parents make all care decisions without the teen's input
PN-S13-15.D: Limiting phone and internet use completely during the hospital stay

PN-S13-16.A: Explain the procedure in detail a full week in advance so the child has time to prepare
PN-S13-16.C: Tell the child that the blood draw won't hurt at all, so there's nothing to fear
PN-S13-16.D: Say nothing about the procedure ahead of time to avoid upsetting the child

PN-S13-19.A: Mix the medication into a full bottle of formula and give it at the next feeding
PN-S13-19.C: Pour it quickly into the back of the throat so the infant swallows it
PN-S13-19.D: Give it while the infant is lying flat on the back so it goes down easily

PN-S13-20.A: "Use scented baby wipes to clean the diaper area thoroughly at each diaper change."
PN-S13-20.C: "Change the diaper only when it's heavily soiled, to avoid irritating the skin with frequent changes."
PN-S13-20.D: "Apply a heavy layer of cornstarch powder to the diaper area at every change."

PN-S13-22.A: "Give the daily dose at bedtime, after your child has brushed their teeth."
PN-S13-22.C: "Stop the medication on school days and give it only on weekends."
PN-S13-22.D: "Crush the extended-release tablets and mix them into applesauce."

PN-S13-23.A: "Please try to stay strong for your child. Your child needs you to be strong right now."
PN-S13-23.C: "Leukemia is very treatable these days, so there's really no need to worry so much."
PN-S13-23.D: "You should ask the doctor about your concerns when they come back."
